title: Pullman's stable, as its 1890s photographs show it
items: The stable at the east end of 1729 Prairie, beside the palm house, is no longer a plain draft box. Its steep slate roof rises from the first-floor cornice to a flat deck ringed with iron cresting, with a domed lantern on top. The upper storey on 18th Street rises through the roof as one long wall of small windows. Below it are an arcade of round arches and a polygonal bay of round-headed windows, with a tall chimney at the east end. A square belvedere with a balustrade stands where the palm-house range meets the stable.
